biography.plain_text: Leo Liebowitz was an American businessman who co-founded the company that became Getty Realty. He built a gasoline distribution business whose retained properties later formed a national real estate investment trust. Its portfolio focused on convenience stores and automotive retail sites. He retired as chairman in 2021, shortly before his death.

long_biography.plain_text:
Getty Realty co-founder Leo Liebowitz entered the fuel business as a station lessee after working as a mechanic for the City of New York. Born in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, to immigrant parents, he began with a leased Sunoco station and then added another location. Operating these small businesses gave him the starting point for a much larger network, assembled through partnerships and acquisitions.

Liebowitz also developed ways to involve employees in the business beyond their daily work. His holiday gift programme distributed Getty shares to staff, giving them a personal stake in the company. Alongside his corporate responsibilities, he served as president of the Society of Independent Gasoline Marketers of America, representing the industry in which he had built his career.

uncertainties: Source Alive and birth year 1928 conflict with the verified death announcement and detailed memorial. Corrections are proposed, with 28 September 1927 to 12 December 2021 as the researched dates. Inventory categories retain the immutable Alive baseline even though mortality research establishes death.

Terminal classifications use December 2021. SEC filings near death establish substantial retained founder economics, but no full estate schedule or exact terminal portfolio valuation was found. Primary Real Estate and Founder are bounded inferences rather than current 2026 roles.

Schedule 13G/A includes shares over which he shared control but disclaimed beneficial ownership. The Form 4 distinguishes his sole-beneficiary revocable trust from spouse, family and charity interests. No aggregate share count is converted into a personal net-worth estimate.

Energy origin and Real Estate primary are intentionally different: the commercial model shifted from fuel marketing to property ownership. Original lease finance and family capital are unresolved, so broad Self-made is used without an independent-start claim.

Full memorial notices were available through indexed page extracts, including the exact birth and early career account and the signed Cooper remembrance. Direct Legacy requests later failed, including a 403 response. These are identified memorial sources, not anonymous snippets or independent newspaper investigations; promotional character praise is excluded.

No verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram, website, Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, Vimeo, Flickr or TikTok profile was located in exact-name searches and linked source review. No person-specific Wikipedia or Forbes profile was found. The only proposed web profile is the verified company website; corporate social accounts are not substituted.

Middle names, secondary nationality and secondary residence were not established. No name is fabricated from initials or identity-adjacent directory records. Birth/death age fields remain system-derived.

The source vessel relationship extends to February 2026 after his death; it is not used to contradict mortality or assert current personal ownership. ICIJ supplies only a historical identity bridge and does not imply unlawful conduct.

Corporate tax-evasion allegations encountered in secondary searches were checked against United States v. Rea. That judgment concerns Getty Terminals and named individual defendants, not Liebowitz. No personal conviction or participation is asserted. The company-level controversy is retained as research context without assigning him unsupported culpability.

The company history identifies a 1955 co-founding platform, while the memorial distinguishes an earlier leased station and a later Power Test acquisition. Exact early transaction dates are omitted from published prose; the partner was Milton Safenowitz, distinct from friend and director Milton Cooper.
